next_step: Schedule scale test: full-day developer load on dedicated pool; finalize SLA language
notes:
Account background: HexStack makes an IDE-integrated copilot focused on professional developer teams (plugin across JetBrains + VS Code). Early traction with ~250 engineers across multiple customers; building team features (multi-file edits, live code actions, CI-aware suggestions).

Commercial ask: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput during peak dev hours (09:00-18:00 PT). They need guaranteed low tail latency for streaming completions (<60ms per token on average for 1k concurrent streams) and deterministic cost for monthly forecasting. Want burst policy for overnight spikes (CI-run bursts) with predictable credit usage.

Technical constraints / preferences:
- Model/version pinning mandatory: will pin to a Roberta-family fine-tuned + safety adapters; need ability to stage model rollout (canary then full).
- Streaming: token-level streaming to the editor with resumable connections for flaky mobile connections.
- Keystroke-level latency target: sub-50ms ideal for single-token ops; acceptable up to 80ms for complex multi-token completions.
- Tokenization and prefix caching: want prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated context costs across repeated repo patterns.
- Throughput shape: heavy daytime interactive traffic (peak 9k-12k tokens/sec across pool), nightly CI bursts up to 3x baseline for 1-2 hours.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must integrate with company SSO (Okta SAML) and central KMS for key wrapping.
- EU data residency for EU customers; global accounts may have mixed residency — want per-customer residency controls.
- Audit logging and retention settings required (90 days standard, 1-year on request).

POC plan and timeline:
- Week 0: Technical kickoff + security questionnaire (done 2026-02-28).
- Week 1-2: Pilot cluster provisioned in dedicated pool (redwood-ded-hex-1), limited to 50 devs — smoke test streaming and pinning.
- Week 3: Load test day (2026-03-12) with simulated 500 concurrent editors; measure p50/p95/p99 latency, KV cache hit rates.
- Week 4: Cost tune with Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching / quantization guidance).
- Decision: expand to full team if p95 latency < 120ms and burst policy met.

Recent interactions (timeline):
- 2026-02-25: Intro call — AE Maya Chen + SE Luca; demo of Dedicated features. (fireflies: ff_20260225_intro_hex)
- 2026-02-28: Security questionnaire submitted; Redwood provided initial answers (drive link above).
- 2026-03-02: Deep technical session on streaming and model pinning; followed by quick follow-up email with suggested rollout configs.
- 2026-03-08: Pricing discussion — interested in 12-month reserved capacity + burst credits. AE sent draft SOW.

Quotes / snippets from the customer:
- "We need keystroke-level predictability for our dev experience — spikes are harmful."
- "Pinning and staged rollouts are non-negotiable; can't have silent model drift."

Next steps (short):
- Confirm load test scope and synthetic workload (SE + HexStack infra).
- Legal to review residency clause; provide Redwood's standard data residency appendix.
- Finalize reserved capacity size and burst credit cost model.

Sales ops notes:
- Suggested initial commit: 2x A100-equivalent reserved nodes with autoscale to 3x for bursts; include Optimize engagement for 3 months.
- Upside: platform integration with HexStack telemetry could drive embed upsell (embeddings for repo search).

Internal action items:
- SE Luca to produce detailed load profile template by 2026-03-10.
- AE Maya to loop in Legal for residency appendix and privacy addendum.
- Solutions: prepare canary rollback policy examples and SLO language for contract.
